title: Page of Pentacles Tarot Meaning: Upright & Reversed
description: Page of Pentacles upright: learning, opportunity, practicality; reversed: plans on paper. Love, work, money, advice and Waite's 1911 text. Ask your question.
h1: Page of Pentacles Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: Page of Pentacles, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a young page in a green tunic and red hood stands in a flowering field, holding up a single pentacle in both hands and gazing at it.
capsule: The Page of Pentacles means learning, opportunity and practicality: a new skill, course or job taken up with patient ambition. Reversed, plans stay on paper or focus slips before anything takes root. A steady, encouraging card, it prefers small finished steps to big plans. Its answer is yes, since the Page is already studying the coin in his hands.

blocks.heading: What is on the Page of Pentacles card?
paragraphs: A young page stands in a green field and gazes at one coin held up before his face. Waite describes "a youthful figure, looking intently at the pentacle which hovers over his raised hands" (p. 260). Waite also says the Page "moves slowly, insensible of that which is about him" (p. 260): for him nothing exists but the coin.

On the 1909 card the sky is yellow, and the page wears a green tunic with a pale sash, tan boots and a red hood whose long scarf hangs down at his side. The coin does seem to float just above his open palms. Behind him are a clump of trees on the left, a ploughed brown field and a blue mountain on the right, and small red and yellow flowers in the grass; the bottom reads PAGE of PENTACLES. His standing figure fills most of the card.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the Page of Pentacles?
paragraphs: Waite's list for the Page (p. 260) puts study first: application, scholarship and reflection, then news and the person who brings it, then rule and management. Waite's reversed side (p. 260) leans toward spending too freely: prodigality, dissipation, luxury, and unfavourable news.

blocks.heading: What does the Page of Pentacles mean upright?
paragraphs: Learning comes first with this card: a student's attention turned toward something real and useful. The Page of Pentacles often appears when a practical opportunity opens up, such as a course, an apprenticeship, a first job, a side project or a plan to save, and you stand at the very start, curious and willing to work.

Practicality and quiet ambition go together here. The Page does not daydream about the coin; he studies it. Progress may be slow, but each small step adds to something you can hold in your hands. What would you like to master, and what is the first lesson?

blocks.heading: What does the Page of Pentacles mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, the card can point to procrastination and plans on paper: the course bought and never started, the budget written and never followed. A lack of focus may let learning slip before it takes root, and self-doubt can stop you before you begin, waiting until you feel ready or clever enough.
Waite's reversed list, with prodigality and luxury (p. 260), adds a money side: spending on comfort instead of on the goal. Choose one practical step, keep it small enough to finish, and complete it.

blocks.heading: What does the Page of Pentacles mean in love?
paragraphs: Love grows slowly here, the way the Page handles his coin: with attention and care. The card favors courtship built on reliability, small practical gestures and keeping your word, whether you are getting to know someone or tending a bond of many years. Without a partner, it suits taking time to learn what you really want in a partner.
Reversed, interest may stay half-hearted, plans to meet may keep slipping, or love may wait while study or work take everything. Let your care take a simple, tangible form.

blocks.heading: What does the Page of Pentacles mean for work and money?
paragraphs: A coin held up for study fits the early stage of a career: training, an internship, a new job, a certificate, learning a trade. Money shows up as modest beginnings with this Page: a first income, a new savings habit, learning to budget, or a small opportunity that needs patience to grow. Reversed, it can mean careless spending or a money plan that never gets started.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the Page of Pentacles?
paragraphs: Start learning one practical skill, even with a single short lesson. Pick something you could use in everyday life, find one good resource, and set aside the first hour for it.

blocks.heading: Is the Page of Pentacles a yes or no card?
The Page of Pentacles as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: The young figure studying a single coin on the Page of Pentacles is a student or beginner of any age: diligent, curious, grounded and a little serious, someone who learns by doing and keeps promises. Put in terms of feelings, the card means sincere but careful interest: steady affection, the wish to go slowly and to show care through actions rather than grand words, sometimes with shyness about saying it. Reversed, those feelings are unsure or slow to grow, with interest that does not turn into action, or attention pulled away by other priorities.

blocks.heading: The Page of Pentacles with other cards

pairs.text: A practical opportunity and the patience to learn it. A good start to build on.
From first lesson to steady practice: the beginner becoming skilled.
Skill and a plan meet; you have what you need to begin.
Studying while juggling other duties. Keep the schedule simple.

blocks.heading: Page of Pentacles or Knight of Pentacles?
paragraphs: Waite gives the Knight of Pentacles a slow, heavy horse and has him show his coin without looking at it (p. 258); the modern reading is diligence, routine and slow progress.
The Page looks closely at the coin because everything about it is still new; the Knight already knows the work and simply carries on. One is learning, the other is doing.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the Page of Pentacles
paragraphs: What practical skill would make my life easier?
Which plan of mine has stayed on paper too long?
What is one small step I can finish today?

faq.q: Is the Page of Pentacles a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good. It is an encouraging card about learning and practical chances, with nothing threatening in it. Reversed, it is a nudge rather than a warning: the plan is fine, it only needs a first real step.

faq.q: Does the Page of Pentacles mean a new job?
faq.a: It can. Among its modern meanings are a job offer, an internship or training that opens a door, and Waite's list also gives news and messages (p. 260). It does not promise a particular offer; it describes the start of something practical that grows with effort.

faq.q: Is the Page of Pentacles a man or a woman?
faq.a: Either. Waite writes of "a youthful figure" and calls the Page "he" (p. 260), but in a reading this Page is a role: a learner, a newcomer to a field or a beginner in a new job, whoever that is. Sometimes it is not a person at all but a piece of news or a practical chance.

waite.quote: Application, study, scholarship, reflection; another reading says news, messages and the bringer thereof; also rule, management. Reversed: Prodigality, dissipation, liberality. luxury; unfavourable news.
